question.worked_solution:
The multiplicative property of modular congruences states that if

$$
a≡b\,\text{and}\,c≡d\,(\text{mod}\,n),
$$

then, we have 

$$
ac≡bd\,(\text{mod}\,n).
$$

First, we note the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}113 & ≡11\cdot 10+3\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡11\cdot 0+3\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡3\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\ 119 & ≡11\cdot 10+9\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡11\cdot 0+9\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡9\, & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the multiplicative property of congruences, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}113\cdot 119 & ≡3\cdot 9\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡27\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡2\cdot 10+7\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡2\cdot 0+7\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0+7\, & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡7\, & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
113\cdot 119\text{ mod }10=7.
$$
